text:
Philip Rubin is an American scientist and educator known for his interdisciplinary research on embodied cognition, speech production, and language. He earned a Bachelor of Arts in psychology and linguistics from Brandeis University and a PhD in experimental psychology from the University of Connecticut under the supervision of Michael Turvey, Ignatius Mattingly, Philip Lieberman, and Alvin Liberman. Rubin's research combines computational, engineering, linguistic, physiological, and psychological approaches to understand the biological basis of speech and language.
He is best known for his work on articulatory synthesis, including the development of the ASY and SWS systems, which model the physiology and acoustics of speech production. He also developed the HADES signal processing system and the SPIEL programming language, a predecessor of MATLAB. Rubin has contributed significantly to the theoretical understanding of speech production, introducing a dynamical systems perspective that emphasizes spatiotemporal coordination of speech events, such as the "dances of the vocal tract."
Rubin has held leadership roles in science policy and administration, including serving as Director of the Division of Behavioral and Cognitive Sciences at the National Science Foundation (NSF) and as a senior advisor in the Directorate for Social, Behavioral, and Economic Sciences. He was the co-founder and first President of AVISA, the Auditory-Visual Speech Association, and has been involved in science advocacy, including work on human subjects research and ethical issues in emerging technologies.
He has also contributed to the development of educational models and has been active in science policy, serving on various boards and committees, including the National Academy of Public Administration and the Federation of Associations in Behavioral and Brain Sciences (FABBS). Rubin is a Fellow of the Acoustical Society of America, the American Association for the Advancement of Science, the American Psychological Association, and the American Psychological Society, among others.
In addition to his scientific work, Rubin is a photographer and has exhibited work focusing on urban wall art, graffiti, and painted buildings. He is married to Joette Katz, and they have two children. He is recognized for his contributions to science, education, and public policy, and has received numerous awards and honors for his work in science and technology.
